$comment: Where each engine op is answered when the engine's JavaScript does not run beside its ops.
WHY THIS EXISTS. On iOS Performance+ content JavaScript and the engine's JavaScript API
layer -- WebGL, Canvas2D, migo.* -- run in a Worker inside WebKit's WebContent process, and
the ops they call are implemented in Rust in the host process. deno_core is not there to
dispatch them. Every op therefore needs a decided answer to one question -- where is this
call answered -- and the answer decides its latency, its failure mode and what it costs per
frame. Written once, here, it is the single source both halves are generated or checked from:
the producer's op shim and the host's decoders.
HOW IT IS CHECKED. The op list is DERIVED by scripts/lib/runtime_ops.py from the
deno_core::extension! registrations and the engine's `ext:core/ops` imports; this file
supplies only the classification. An op the engine's JavaScript imports that is not
classified here fails the gate, and so does a classification for an op nothing imports, an
op filed under the wrong extension, or a lane whose shape the op's Rust signature
contradicts. See scripts/test-runtime-op-boundary-contract.sh.
An entry is a lane name, or an object when a stream or command op returns a value: then
`local_answer` says what the producer answers with, because the host's answer arrives too late
to be the return value.

lanes.local: Answered in the producer without crossing: producer-owned state, a host snapshot injected at start and kept current by events, or a pure computation.
lanes.stream: Encoded into the frame command stream and executed by the host, in order, when the frame's packet is decoded. No answer crosses back.
lanes.command: Sent as an ordered control message outside the frame. No answer crosses back; a failure is reported by event, not thrown.
lanes.sync: Crosses the synchronous barrier: the Worker blocks in one request to the content origin until the host answers.
lanes.async: Returns a promise settled by a host reply on the downlink.
lanes.unsupported: Not offered by the Performance+ profile. The producer throws a stable not-supported error, and capability queries report the feature absent.

host_v8_ad.reason: Ads are the host app's integration with its ad SDK, as on every platform: whether it has one is asked once, synchronously, and each ad's lifecycle -- create, load, show, hide, restyle, destroy -- is a command through the host-service channel, whose events reach content through the hooks the embedded runtime calls.

host_v8_audio.reason: Audio plays on the host (PCM never crosses the process boundary; control messages do). A decode is adopted on the host as the AudioBuffer's PCM, so its samples cross only when content reads its channels (materialize, synchronous) or starts a buffer it wrote. Graph edits and parameter changes are ordered commands; analyser reads and decodes are awaited; creation that can fail in a way content catches is synchronous, and so is setInnerAudioOption, whose refusal is what its facade reports as fail. Recording needs the microphone, which the profile does not grant.

host_v8_base.reason: Package loading reads the host's mounted code, synchronously where `require` is synchronous; callback ids are the producer's. Heap statistics are V8's, and content here runs in WebKit's JavaScriptCore, which exposes none to a page: a number the host made up would read as a measurement, so the call is refused.

host_v8_console.reason: Console output is diagnostics routed to the host's log, in order.

host_v8_device.reason: Vibration, the display wake lock and network monitoring are host commands. The battery and the network type are the host's last report, read synchronously: the network changes during a session, so the host's one copy is the answer rather than a snapshot the producer would have to keep in step. The local address is read from the system by the engine in the host's process, synchronously, as the embedded op reads it: WebContent has no view of the device's interfaces. The clipboard, location, the screen's brightness, capture and recording state, code scanning and the motion sensors are the host app's services: each request is a command the host makes the embedded op's scope check and device-service call for (engine/crates/core/src/runtime/service_channel.rs), and its result, a refusal included, and every reading reach content through the hooks the embedded runtime calls. Orientation is fixed when the session starts (its size is). Turning the debugging aids on or off is the host's, answered synchronously as the embedded op is, so content's call fails where the host has none and the state it reads next is the new one.

host_v8_file.reason: The sandboxed file system is the host's. The synchronous API is the barrier and the asynchronous one is awaited, preserving which calls content may block on. Saving a file to the player's disk is the host app's save dialog, awaited while the path is resolved through the game's sandbox.

host_v8_image.reason: Images decode on the host, where the texture they become lives, so loads are awaited; ids are the producer's.

op_destroy_image.local_answer: whether the id was live, which the producer allocated and tracks

host_v8_lifecycle.reason: Exit and restart are the host's decisions, requested by command.

host_v8_media.reason: Camera, video and photo-album surfaces are native UI and native permissions, outside the Performance+ profile; so is video decoding, which content is told this profile does not have. Choosing images, media and files is the host app's picker, reached as a command through the host-service channel; the files it hands over are taken into the session's /tmp, as in process. Compressing, previewing and saving to the album name content's files: they are awaited, because the host resolves each path through the game's sandbox into a file the app can open before it asks (migo_services::host_paths, as the embedded ops do), and a refusal fails the call. Recording the game (getGameRecorder) is the native renderer's frames through an encoder beside it, which the Performance+ profile does not have yet.

host_v8_network.reason: Requests are made by the host, not by WebContent's fetch: the engine's network API has no CORS, carries the host's TLS and domain policy, and has sockets the web platform does not. Starts and reads are awaited; closes and cancels are commands. The handle an upload is aborted through is synchronous because it names a host resource -- the upload streams a file the host opened -- and content is given it before it awaits the upload.

host_v8_payment.reason: In-app purchase is the host app's store integration, not the engine's: whether its store allows paying is asked synchronously, a request reaches it as a command through the host-service channel, and its result reaches content through the hook the embedded runtime calls.

host_v8_share.reason: Sharing is the host app's: the share menu's state is set as a command through the host-service channel, and a share -- to the app's chooser, to a friend, from the image menu, or the menu's reply -- is awaited while the host resolves the image it names through the game's sandbox (migo_services::host_paths), as the embedded ops do.

host_v8_storage.reason: Key-value storage is the host's, so it survives a WebContent termination; synchronous and asynchronous forms keep their shapes.

host_v8_system.reason: Device, window and system descriptions are an environment snapshot the host injects and updates by event. What the app says about itself (getAppBaseInfo, and the fields of getSystemInfoSync it feeds) is read from the host synchronously: it changes during a session -- the debugging aids turned on, the language or text size changed -- so the host's one copy is the answer. Login, account, permission requests, the settings pages, Bluetooth, beacons and mini-program navigation are the host app's services: each request is a command the host makes the embedded op's scope check and device-service call for (engine/crates/core/src/runtime/service_channel.rs), and its result, a refusal included, and the host's reports reach content through the hooks the embedded runtime calls. Ecosystem calls are awaited while the files a group share names are resolved through the game's sandbox. Whether the host app answers ecosystem calls at all, and the values it reported for the synchronous getters, are the host's, read synchronously: the producer has no host of its own to ask. The scopes content was granted, the app's authorization and the system's switches are the host's last report, read synchronously as the network type is: each changes during a session -- a prompt answered, a setting changed and come back from -- so the host's one copy is the answer. This device as a Bluetooth LE peripheral -- a GATT server centrals connect to, and its advertising -- is outside the Performance+ profile.

host_v8_touch.reason: The soft keyboard is host UI driven by commands; its input returns as events. A gamepad's motors are set by command: the producer times each effect and settles its promise, and the command carries the duration, so nothing needs to answer.

host_v8_ui.reason: Toasts, modals, loading indicators, action sheets and the window's pointer lock and size are the host app's, reached as commands through the host-service channel, with results through the hooks the embedded runtime calls; the menu-button rectangle is layout the environment snapshot carries. The cursor answers synchronously whether the host's window took it, so it crosses the synchronous barrier: the host shapes the request as the embedded op does (migo_services::cursor), an image resolved through the game's sandbox.

host_v8_update.reason: A package update is the host app's: whether it offers them is asked once, synchronously, of the service the embedded op asks, and applying one is a command. The check's result and the download's outcome reach content through the hooks the embedded runtime calls.

host_v8_utility.reason: Text encoding is a pure computation the producer performs.

host_v8_web.reason: Timers and offscreen canvases. Time comes from WebContent's own monotonic clock, which is the clock content's frame timestamps are compared with; canvas lifetime rides the stream so a canvas created mid-frame exists for the draws after it.

op_create_offscreen_canvas.local_answer: the canvas id, allocated by the producer as GL resource ids already are

host_v8_webgl.reason: Rendering. The engine's WebGL and Canvas2D facades already encode state, draws and uniforms into the frame command stream; on Performance+ every call that has no answer the producer lacks joins them there -- resource creation with producer-allocated ids, shader source, uploads, attachments -- so a frame's GL work crosses once, in order, inside its packet. Queries whose answer is the driver's cross the synchronous barrier -- the compressed-texture formats among them, which only the host's renderer knows and knows only once it is up; attributes, the remaining capabilities and id allocation are the producer's own. requestAnimationFrame is the frame clock's request and tick.

op_create_context_2d.local_answer: success: the canvas id is the producer's, and a context the host cannot create is reported as a context-loss event

op_submit_render_stream.local_answer: the stream's own validation status: the producer builds the packet, and a packet the host refuses is answered on the downlink, not here

host_v8_worker.reason: Content already runs in a Worker, and WebKit offers no nested-Worker constructor inside one (confirmed on-device, iPhone 12 / iOS 17.0.3: `typeof Worker === "undefined"` there). migo.createWorker crosses a dedicated MessagePort to the page instead, which a Window context's Worker support has no such gap in -- see worker-relay.mjs and worker-page-relay.mjs.

host_v8_worker_inner.reason: The nested worker the page makes runs its own bootstrap (worker-nested-bootstrap.js) over its native self.postMessage/onmessage, not this shared module -- it has no Rust op boundary to answer for at all, and the in-process lane's audio/network/filesystem capabilities this module also exposes to a worker script are not yet proxied through the page relay either.

$comment: The members of deno_core's `core` object that the engine's JavaScript calls and that are
not ops: `core.read`, `core.close` and `core.tryClose` act on deno's resource table, which
the external execution has no equivalent of. The handles they name are the network
service's (migo_services::network::resources), so on that lane these are answered by the
host exactly as the ops beside them are, and the engine's `ReadableStream` pulls a response
body the same way in both executions.
They are classified here rather than under an extension because the op table is derived
from `deno_core::extension!` registrations and `ext:core/ops` imports, and a core member is
neither. A member on a crossing lane carries a number in service-ops.json; a `local` one is
built in the producer out of the members that do.
